newsitem.title: USA: Gadfly's "draft Tiger" effort fails for DuPont board.
newsitem.headline: Gadfly's "draft Tiger" effort fails for DuPont board.

text.p: Gadfly corporate shareholder Evelyn Davis offered a proposal Wednesday to shake up what she called the "old fogies" on DuPont Co.'s board of directors -- by giving Tiger Woods a seat.
But the effort to make the young golf champion a corporate director came up a few hundred million votes short.

"We have a lot of old fogies on this board," said Davis, who publishes a Washington newsletter and makes a habit of hectoring management at annual meetings of the numerous companies in which she holds stock.

"What we need -- and I'd like to nominate seriously here -- Mr. Tiger Woods," Davis said. "He is a young man, an innovator, who against all odds succeeded, who was motivated. That's what we lack in this company."
"Since this gentleman doesn't know much about business, he could bring unbiased viewpoints," she said. She added she did not have Woods' permission to nominate him.
Not that Woods needed to have worried. When votes were tallied at the end of the meeting, all 13 of the company's incumbent directors were re-elected with more than 99 percent of the votes cast.
There are 579 million DuPont shares outstanding. As for Woods' tally, "he got my 150," Davis said. That, and probably a few hundred more, DuPont Chairman Edgar Woolard estimated.
